title: Arbitrary Breakpoints and Media Queries
subtopics: Using custom media queries where needed
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of arbitrary breakpoints and media queries.
Apply one appropriate technique to a small Tailwind CSS example.
Verify the expected result and identify a common failure mode.

content.intro: In this lesson, focus on arbitrary breakpoints and media queries and connect it to the way Tailwind CSS generates and applies utility styles.
content.why_it_matters: Arbitrary Breakpoints and Media Queries helps you build layouts that remain consistent as content, viewport width and component context change.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum highlights: One-off breakpoint conditions; Width-based media queries; Combining responsive conditions; Using custom media queries where needed. Treat these as practical decisions rather than a list to memorize: identify the intended behavior, choose the smallest suitable utility or directive, and inspect what the browser receives.

items: Using custom media queries where needed

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Arbitrary Breakpoints and Media Queries
content_blocks.code:
<section class="grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3">
  <article class="rounded-xl border p-4">Card A</article>
  <article class="rounded-xl border p-4">Card B</article>
  <article class="rounded-xl border p-4">Card C</article>
</section>
content_blocks.expected_output: Cards stack by default, become two columns at sm, and three columns at lg.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with the example, change one decision related to arbitrary breakpoints and media queries, then compare the outcome. In a Tailwind-enabled project, confirm the generated CSS exists; class strings alone do not make styles available without a configured build.

content_blocks.title: Version and compatibility note
content_blocks.text: This course prioritizes Tailwind CSS v4. Confirm your installed version and use its matching official guide. Snippets using v3 directives or configuration are labelled as legacy and should not be mixed blindly with v4 syntax.

content.task: Create a minimal example demonstrating arbitrary breakpoints and media queries. Include a before/after comparison and explain why the chosen utility, variant or directive is appropriate.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate at least one decision tied to arbitrary breakpoints and media queries.
Keep the example easy to inspect, with complete utility names.
Test the outcome and document one limitation or environment assumption.
hints: Identify which listed syllabus topic is most important to arbitrary breakpoints and media queries.
Change one utility, token, variant or configuration setting at a time.
Inspect generated CSS and computed styles before changing unrelated code.
content.expected_output: Cards stack by default, become two columns at sm, and three columns at lg.
troubleshooting: If no style appears, verify the package, CSS import and build-tool integration before changing the HTML.
If only a state or breakpoint style fails, check the full class token, source detection, condition and computed CSS.
For a framework snippet, import the stylesheet through its supported entry point and consult the current official guide.
common_mistakes: Applying arbitrary breakpoints and media queries without checking generated styles or browser behavior.
Mixing Tailwind v3 and v4 setup examples without a migration plan.
Treating visual appearance as a substitute for semantic markup, keyboard usability or actual component behavior.
summary: Arbitrary Breakpoints and Media Queries is one part of a predictable utility-first styling workflow.
Keep examples small, test the built interface and use version-matched documentation.
